msg1_brief: Use when enrichment found a dated trigger in the last 90 days: announced entry into a new country, a rollout of lockers (výdejní boxy) or pickup points, a funding round, a new country manager or expansion hire, or an acquisition. Open with that trigger in plain words and its month. Then one sentence on why that moment matters for the last mile: in a new market a company starts with no network, systems or brand, and what gets decided in the first months shapes the cost per parcel for years. End with one easy question about where they are with it. Write in Czech with formal address (vykání). Start with 'Dobrý den,' and no name, so there is no vocative or gender to get wrong; no sign-off. Avoid first-person singular past tense ('viděl jsem'); use 'zaujalo mě' or the present tense. Put a noun before the company name ('společnost X', 'firma X') so the name stays in the nominative and the verb agrees with the noun. 2-3 sentences, under 400 characters including the greeting. Must not: flatter or congratulate at length, cite any number or client, list services, ask for a call, say where the news was found, use a trigger older than 90 days, or touch anything private.
